newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Independent's S.African unit's op profit up 19 pct.
newsitem.headline: Independent's S.African unit's op profit up 19 pct.

text.p: Independent Newspapers Plc said on Monday that its 60-percent owned South African subsidiary, Independent Newspapers Holdings Ltd, reported an 18.7 percent rise in operating profit to 124.5 million rand last year.

The operating profit from continuing operations reflected a good improvement in turnover and a healthy increase in the operating margin to 12.6 percent from 12.0 percent in 1995, Independent said in a statement.
Turnover was up by 13.7 percent to 992 million rand with advertising, circulation and commercial printing and publishing activities all showing real growth on 1995 figures.
Pre-tax profit rose by 30.9 percent at 123.6 million rand while earnings per share increased by 24.7 percent to 167.8 cents per share.
A final dividend of 60 cents per share has been declared and will be paid on or about May 20.
The company said it was well positioned to produce further growth.
"Given no unexpected deterioration in economic trends, earnings for 1997 are expected to show further good growth," the company said.
It also said that discussions were taking place relating to INHL's 42.5 percent investment in New Africa Publications Limited, which publishes Sowetan.
